$comment: === EV Incentive Schema ===
Each YAML file in data/incentives/{market}/ describes one government incentive program.
HOW RULES WORK:
- 'rules' is an ordered list. Each rule has an 'amount' (the incentive value in the
program's currency) and optional 'conditions' that a vehicle must satisfy.
- Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom. The FIRST rule whose conditions all match wins.
If no rule matches, the vehicle gets $0 from this program.
- Within a single rule, all conditions are AND'd: every condition must be true.
- A rule with no 'conditions' (or an empty object) matches every vehicle -- useful
as a catch-all fallback at the end of the list.
EXAMPLE -- tiered by segment and price cap:
rules:
- amount: 7500
conditions:
price_local_max: 55000
segments: [sedan, hatchback]
- amount: 7500
conditions:
price_local_max: 80000
segments: [suv, truck, crossover, van]
This gives $7,500 to sedans/hatchbacks under $55k and SUVs/trucks/etc. under $80k.
Anything else (e.g. a $90k SUV) falls through with no match, so it gets $0.
EXAMPLE -- flat rebate with a price cap:
rules:
- amount: 5000
conditions:
price_local_max: 65000
Every vehicle under $65k gets $5,000. Vehicles over $65k get nothing.
EXAMPLE -- unconditional rebate:
rules:
- amount: 3000
No conditions, so every vehicle qualifies for $3,000.
LEVELS:
- Each incentive has a 'level' (e.g. 'Federal', 'State', 'Province', 'Country').
- The UI groups regions by level and enforces single-select within each level.
For example, a US user can pick Federal + one State, but not California + Colorado.
- All regions sharing the same 'level' string are treated as mutually exclusive.
- Level names are freeform per market: 'State' for US, 'Province' for CA, 'Country' for EU.
TIPS FOR CONTRIBUTORS:
- Put more specific rules first (narrow conditions), general rules last.
- To explicitly give $0 to a group, add a rule with amount: 0 and matching conditions.
- Use 'disclaimer' when the real-world amount depends on factors we can't model
(buyer income, lease vs. purchase, etc.). The UI shows this to the user.

id.description: Unique identifier across all incentive files (e.g. 'us-federal-ira')

market.description: Must match the parent directory name (e.g. 'us', 'ca', 'eu')

region.description: 'federal' for country-wide, or a sub-region code (e.g. 'ca' for California, 'qc' for Quebec)

effective_date.description: When the program took effect, YYYY-MM-DD

source.description: Wayback Machine archived URL documenting the program

level.description: Grouping level for mutual exclusivity (e.g. 'Federal', 'State', 'Province'). Only one region per level can be selected.

rules.description: Ordered list of { amount, conditions? } objects -- see HOW RULES WORK above

expiry_date.description: When the program expires, YYYY-MM-DD. null or omitted = ongoing

description.description: Short human-readable summary of the incentive rules, shown in the UI below the region chips

disclaimer.description: Shown in the UI when real-world eligibility depends on factors we can't model

price_local_max.description: Vehicle MSRP must be <= this value

price_local_min.description: Vehicle MSRP must be >= this value

segments.description: Vehicle segment must be in this list. Values: sedan, suv, hatchback, truck, van, crossover

model_years.description: Vehicle model year must be in this list

battery_capacity_kwh_min.description: Vehicle battery capacity must be >= this value
